newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium braced for public sector workers demo.
newsitem.headline: Belgium braced for public sector workers demo.

text.p: Much of Belgium's public sector is expected to shut down on Wednesday afternoon as workers take to the streets of the capital Brussels to warn the government not to tamper with their employment and pension rights.

Some air traffic controllers said they would join the demonstration, threatening to cause delays at Brussels airport, but other forms of transport and post office services were not expected to be affected.

Both train and bus drivers' unions have urged their members not to disrupt services, although spokeswomen for the national railway company and Brussels regional transport authority said they did not rule out isolated cases of action.

Belgium's three main public sector workers unions, which are organising Wednesday's demonstration, represent staff working in Belgian national and local government administrations, as well as transport and communications workers.
The Belgian government is working on plans to limit wage increases in the public sector to 6.1 percent over the next two years, as well as reform of the country's pension and social security system.
Wednesday's demonstration will be the first joint action by the three main unions since they fell out over the government's wage proposals last autumn.
